# bad-repo — planted BAD fixture for the claim gate

The paragraphs below are neutral filler prose. They describe the
shape of the fixture and nothing else. The first claim above carries
no claim-state label anywhere near it, and no banner qualifies this
file, so the gate must name it as unlabeled. The second claim, much
further down, carries a verified label on its own line. That label
is the one the attestation evidence refutes, because the record for
this repository shows a drifted ground truth. Filler exists only to
keep the two planted claims in separate labeling windows, the same
way real documents separate their claims with ordinary prose about
design, usage, provenance, and history. Nothing in these paragraphs
asserts a figure, a capability, or a state. They are scaffolding
for the control, and the control is the point: one unlabeled claim,
one contradicted claim, both named, nothing else flagged. A reader
who scans the whole file top to bottom should be able to point at
each planted claim and say which failure it exists to produce, and
a reader who reads only the gate output should learn the same two
facts without opening the file at all. That symmetry is what makes
the fixture a control rather than an example: the expected output
is written here in prose, and the gate either matches it or the
gate is wrong. The prose in between stays deliberately plain, in
the ordinary register of a project readme, because real readmes
are mostly plain prose and the gate has to work on those too.
